identity: A grade-school Islamic-education (tarbiya islamiyya) worksheet / question bank, printed as an exam sheet with the punctuation stripped. It is not prose at any point. Twenty items, exactly one per <NL>-delimited line: 13 true/false items (a complete proposition followed by the answer pair صح خطأ) and 7 multiple-choice items (a stem that breaks off mid-construction, followed by exactly three one-word options). Content is grade-1/2 aqida and Quran etiquette: the Kaaba, the names of God, the Fatiha, adab of recitation, wudu, the supplication on entering the lavatory.
law: Exam genre, so doctrine 0e decides granularity before any syntax: the native unit is THE STEM AND EACH OPTION (I2/I3), never the clause and never the printed line. (1) The stem ends where the options begin, even mid-construction; a dangling mudaf, a dangling fronted predicate, or a dangling copula is a colon in disguise (I2 = H1). (2) Every option is its own unit however short, because options are exchangeable answer-siblings; the short-tail brake 0b is suspended here (I3/I4/0f). (3) An option-internal waw is bare-noun waw and never cuts (I5). The <NL> grid hands me the item boundary for free, so my entire job is inside the item, and PASS 2 of the checklist has almost nothing to do: there are only two waw in the whole document and both are bare-noun conjuncts.
reasoning: THE ONE REAL DECISION, and it governs 46 of my 67 boundaries. The competing reading is the-line-is-the-unit (0e corollary, the unobservable printed line): 20 lines, 20 units, every boundary falling on a mandatory pre-<NL> slot and nothing internal. I reject it, and the 3-option lines are what kill it. Line 4 (@27-@33) cannot be one sentence: three bare direction-nouns juxtaposed with no connective and no syntax to hold them; same for the three prophet names at @122-@124 and the three adjectives at @138-@140. So the line is demonstrably NOT the unit here, and once that is established the true/false lines have no defence left. || THE STEM CUT ON MCQ LINES (@30, @47, @88, @96, @121, @129, @137). Every one ends mid-construction, which is my most mechanical law. @30 ittijah, @88 tariq, @96 kalam and @121 sayyidina are mudaf heads waiting for a mudaf ilayh; @137 bi-niam waits for its adjective; @47 waradat and @129 al-Quran close a fronted min-predicate waiting for its subject. This is exactly I2 (a question ending in a trailing fi / huwa / li) and H1 (a stem ending mid-construction with parallel items after it). Confidence hi. @50 kilahuma (both of them) as a third option is independent proof that line 6 is a 3-option MCQ and not a statement. || THE STEM CUT ON TRUE/FALSE LINES (13x, e.g. @5, @39, @146). Stronger than the MCQ case, not weaker: in an MCQ the option at least completes the stem syntax, whereas here the proposition is already grammatically complete and the answer pair cannot attach to it at all. They are the printed answer options, not constituents. Confidence hi. || THE SPLIT BETWEEN THE TWO ANSWER OPTIONS (13x, marked med, my one honest uncertainty). For: I3 is unconditional (every option is its own unit, one word or not); I4 detection fires (two one-word antonymic siblings, zero connectives, recurring in identical position 13 times, i.e. maximal parallelism, and parallelism forces cuts per B2/E1); 0f asks whether the items are exchangeable answers/targets (split) or complementary cells of one record (merge), and a true/false pair is the paradigm exchangeable answer pair, not a term+gloss row like J4; and consistency demands it, since I cannot split north/east/west into three while binding the answer pair into one. Against: only the unobservable layout, since the pair is probably printed side by side with checkboxes. But 0e's corollary explicitly orders me not to let that residue make me timid, my calibration prior is 7:1 toward over-merging, and checklist v2 step 5 makes CUT the default I must argue my way out of. I cannot argue my way out, so I cut. The cost is symmetric either way (13 false cuts vs 13 misses), which is precisely the situation where the prior should decide. || THE TWO WAW, both no-cut. @81 (bi-adab wa-khushu) and @113/@114 (al-ashjar wa al-bihar) are bare nouns with no verb, no participle, no PP frame and no subject of their own, hanging off the same predicate (yaqra, khaliq). The conjunct-weight test says merge; this is the wa-al-Iraq wa-Australia case, and I5 says an option-internal waw never cuts. The standalone waw token at @113 is a spacing artefact and changes nothing. || LINE 11 vs LINE 13, the trap I checked for. @88 huwa tariq dangles (mudaf) and takes three options; @105 huwa al-tariq al-sahih is a complete predicate followed by the answer pair. Nearly identical openings, different item types; the presence of the answer pair is the reliable discriminator, and the definiteness of al-tariq confirms it. || LINE 17 checked the same way. I considered reading bi-niam kathira as a finished statement with only two options after it, but every other MCQ here has exactly three, and many/few/light is the symmetric triple. Internal regularity wins: cut at @137. || NO INTERNAL CUTS ELSEWHERE. @46 allati and @142 alladhi are tight relatives, @159 an is a tight subordinator, and my table says never cut after these. @145 yanal is the predicate of the alladhi subject, not a new asyndetic clause, so D3 does not fire. @151 ghufranaka is quoted content staying attached to its speech verb aqulu (E3). @158 is an OCR variant of yajib and needs no special handling. Items 9, 16, 18 and 20 are factually false statements (six verses not seven, play as an adab, evil from recitation, wudu after prayer); that is the true/false design and never a segmentation signal.
